transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-11 15:30 PT / Duration: 52m / Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Luca Morales (Redwood CSM), Dr. Emily Carter (Acme Head of AI), Mark Ruiz (Platform Eng), Sara Kim (Compliance), Jason Holt (Product)

Summary: quick intro, scope, what counts as success, workload numbers, bench plan, timelines, compliance items and who owns next steps.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick intro from our side — I'm Jordan, I'm the AE on this account, Priya is our solutions engineer, Luca on success.
[00:10] Dr. Emily Carter: Hi all, Emily here. Our goal today is to figure out what mode makes sense for a POC: hosted, dedicated, or private. We have strict latency needs for triage flows and tight compliance for PHI.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Great, thanks Emily. Quick agenda: 1) success criteria 2) workload sizing & traffic profile 3) benchmark plan 4) security/compliance checklist 5) timelines and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:30] Mark Ruiz: Sounds good. I'll try to stay focused on qps and infra questions.
[00:35] Sara Kim: I'll jump in on the compliance bits. We need SOC2 plus KMS integration and data residency in us-east for now.

--- Topics: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, timelines, deployment decision criteria ---

[03:00] Jordan Lee: To start, can you share the high-level success criteria for the POC? What would make this a go/no-go internally?
[03:15] Dr. Emily Carter: Two things: latency — 95th percentile under 400ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), and end-to-end decision latency under 600ms for our triage pipeline. And secondly, quality — our acceptable regression threshold is less than 5% drop vs our baseline on the evaluation set. Cost is secondary but still important — we want a tangible number per 1k tokens.
[03:40] Jason Holt: Also vendor stability and auditability — we can't have logging gaps.

[05:00] Priya Nair: Good. From an infra perspective we need: qps profile (avg, peak), token distribution (mean input tokens, mean output tokens), and whether you need real-time streaming or can batch. Mark, do you have numbers?
[05:20] Mark Ruiz: Baseline: avg 40 qps, burst to 250 qps during peak hours. Typical input size 60 tokens, typical output 120 tokens, but for some notes it goes up to 1k tokens. We do some streaming in the UI for long responses.
[05:50] Priya Nair: Perfect that helps. For a hosted POC we can usually support that but bursts to 250 qps might push costs up if we don't have a burstable dedicated pool. If you want predictable throughput and consistent 95p latency we'd usually recommend Dedicated. Private is mostly about compliance and on-prem constraints.

[07:30] Dr. Emily Carter: We have PHI so private or dedicated with VPC/KMS are on the table. Sara, from compliance?
[07:40] Sara Kim: SOC2 is mandatory. The data residency requirement is us-east only for now. We need KMS/HSM key control ideally — if hosted doesn't support customer-managed KMS we can't use it for production. Also audit logs for all request/response metadata, and retention controls.
[08:10] Jordan Lee: Redwood's hosted API supports encryption at rest and in transit; we have an enterprise plan that supports customer-managed KMS and extended audit logs. For the strictest interpretation of 'customer controls keys' we often recommend Private or Dedicated with a VPC peering + KMS integration.
[08:35] Sara Kim: Ok, so hosted might still be possible if you can offer CMK and audit logs. We'll need the security pack to review.

[10:00] Priya Nair: On benchmarking — our suggested approach: 1) run the same seed prompts against a Redwood-hosted endpoint (single-tenant vs multi-tenant) to gather latency and token costs; 2) run on a Dedicated sizing sim with expected concurrency to validate 95p latency; 3) optional Private on-prem pilot if network or data residency blocks hosted. We'll provide harness and instructions.
[10:30] Mark Ruiz: How intrusive is the harness? We want to avoid sending real PHI to a hosted environment for the first run.
[10:40] Priya Nair: Totally understood. We typically recommend redacting or synthetic data that matches your token distributions. We also can run bench runs inside a Dedicated environment where data never leaves your VPC if you choose Dedicated with private networking. For hosted we can accept synthetic payloads.

[12:00] Jordan Lee: Can we talk throughput sizing? For your avg 40 qps / peak 250 qps with 60/120 token distribution — a rough Dedicated recommendation would be one 8-GPU pool for baseline, scaling to two pools or burst capacity for peaks, depending on model size. Priya, want to add?
[12:20] Priya Nair: Yeah, model choice matters a lot. If you use a 70B quantized model your per-token latency and GPU requirement jumps vs a 13B or an optimized MISTRAL-like opt. We should pick a candidate model family during the POC so we can size properly. Also batching and KV cache for streaming long conversations will help.
[12:50] Mark Ruiz: We expect to use an LLM tuned for clinical summarization, maybe a 13B variant. Latency is critical for the triage flow so maybe 13B with optimizations.

[14:00] Dr. Emily Carter: Quality: we have a labeled eval set — about 5k examples — we'll use that to measure regression and also run manual blind evals. Priya, can you take that as part of the benchmark plan?
[14:15] Priya Nair: Yes, please share a sample of the eval (synthetic or redacted). We'll run automated metrics plus human eval instructions. We'll look at accuracy, hallucination rates, and token cost.

[15:30] Jordan Lee: Let's cover cost signals briefly. Hosted tends to be cheapest for low sustained usage but cost grows with scale; Dedicated gives predictable unit cost per token and helps with high throughput; Private has additional TCO for infra and ops. Typical decision criteria we see: 1) Compliance/keys/data residency => Private/Dedicated, 2) throughput predictability and latency SLO => Dedicated, 3) fastest path to production and experimentation => Hosted.
[16:10] Jason Holt: For the POC we want to test both Hosted (to see raw model outputs and ease) and Dedicated (to validate latency & throughput). If cost isn't crazy we might run both in parallel.

[18:00] Priya Nair: Technically we can run a two-track POC: 1) hosted functional check using synthetic data and eval set for quality, 2) Dedicated load tests with redacted data to validate 95p latency and scaling. We'll produce a report that compares latency, cost, and any regressions.
[18:30] Mark Ruiz: Timeline: we need results in two weeks to inform an executive decision. Is that feasible?
[18:40] Priya Nair: Two weeks is tight but doable for a scoped POC: week 1 set up and run hosted functional tests + seed benchmarks, week 2 run Dedicated sizing and load tests, then compile results. We'll need your sample eval and qps telemetry by tomorrow ideally.

[20:00] Sara Kim: On security docs — can you send SOC2 attestation, pen test summary, and details on KMS and logging? Also SLA and data retention controls.
[20:15] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll share the security pack. For Hosted enterprise customers we have CMK support and extended logs; for Dedicated and Private you get more control by default. I'll include the specifics in the packet.

[22:00] Dr. Emily Carter: A few edge questions: what happens if the Dedicated pool is overloaded? Do you have fallback policies?
[22:15] Priya Nair: We have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or to Hosted in some architectures. For Dedicated customers we can configure overflow/burst strategies. We'll document fallbacks and how they affect SLAs.

[24:30] Jason Holt: How about model versioning and rollouts? We need to be able to pin a model and roll forward if a regression occurs.
[24:45] Priya Nair: Redwood supports model version pinning, canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic rollback triggers based on eval metrics. We'll include the rollout docs in the pack.

[27:00] Mark Ruiz: Networking: if we go Dedicated with VPC peering, what's the typical network setup? Do we need special firewall rules?
[27:15] Jordan Lee: Usually VPC peering + private IPs, TLS between endpoints, and we recommend allowing egress to Redwood control plane for metrics/management. If you need air-gapped Private deployment we have an on-prem option but that adds time to provision.

[29:00] Sara Kim: On keys — can Dedicated integrate with our AWS KMS CMKs so keys never leave our account?
[29:10] Priya Nair: Yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS via an integration. For Private on-prem we offer HSM options in certain packages. We'll send the KMS integration guide.

[31:30] Jordan Lee: Decision criteria recap: Hosted = fastest to try, lower upfront cost, limited CMK unless enterprise plan. Dedicated = predictable latency and throughput, supports CMK and VPC, recommended for steady high qps. Private = for full control, strictest compliance and data residency, higher TCO and longer lead time.

[33:00] Dr. Emily Carter: That matches our internal thinking. For the POC let's do: hosted functional eval with synthetic/sampled data, and Dedicated sizing & load test with redacted data. We'll make the final decision based on latency, quality threshold <5% regression, and a target cost per 1k tokens under $0.20 (rough target for execs).

[34:10] Priya Nair: Noted — we'll draft a benchmark plan with target metrics and a runbook. For the Dedicated sizing we'll propose a 1x pool baseline and show scaling to 2x for peak bursts.

[36:00] Mark Ruiz: One more technical — do you do KV cache warmups for conversation flows? We have a lot of repeated context across sessions.
[36:10] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood supports KV/prefix caching and continuous batching which helps with cost and latency for repeated contexts. We'll include cache behavior notes for the benchmarking doc.

[38:00] Jason Holt: Who from Redwood will be our technical point during the POC?
[38:05] Jordan Lee: Priya will lead the technical POC, Luca will manage on the success side, and I'll coordinate pricing and contracts.

[40:00] Priya Nair: For deliverables: I'll provide the harness + runbook, the seed prompts, and a template results sheet. Jordan will send pricing and Dedicated sizing estimates.

[42:00] Sara Kim: Also please include any attestations around SOC2, ISO, and your pen test cadence. If possible include a redacted pen test executive summary.

[43:30] Jordan Lee: We'll include the security pack and an electronic NDA if needed.

[45:00] Dr. Emily Carter: Timeline recap: sample eval + qps telemetry by 2026-03-12, Priya's harness by 2026-03-13, hosted runs and reporting day 1-3, Dedicated load tests day 4-8, results compiled by 2026-03-25 for exec review. Is that aligned?
[45:25] Priya Nair: Yes we can try to hit that schedule. We'll confirm exact dates in a follow-up email.

[47:00] Jordan Lee: Anything else?
[47:10] Mark Ruiz: Is there a cost for a Dedicated POC environment?
[47:20] Jordan Lee: We often provide a time-limited Dedicated POC at a reduced rate or credit depending on contract progression; Jordan: I'll include options in the pricing doc.

[49:00] Priya Nair: Ok if no further items we can close and I'll send the benchmark plan after the call.
[49:10] Dr. Emily Carter: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the harness.
[49:20] Sara Kim: Thanks.
[49:30] Jason Holt: Thanks.
[49:40] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the pack and action items.

[51:00] Call ended.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlaps, some product names transcribed as 'Redwood Dedi' or 'KV cahce'. References to documents: security pack (link pending), benchmark harness (link to be shared).
